A slow week in Oslo, by train and on foot

Written by Teodor Berg
I took the night train north, which is slower than flying, of course, but it arrives in the middle of the city, and you wake up to snow, pine forests and the sound of the conductor walking past with coffee.
Oslo is small enough to cross on foot in an afternoon, so I left the tram passes in my bag and walked everywhere, from the opera house roof down to the harbour, then up through the old wooden houses of Damstredet.
The museums are excellent, but the best part of the week was the evenings, when the light lasted far longer than I expected, and the whole city seemed to sit outside with blankets, books and thermos flasks.
If you go, pack good shoes, a warm hat and patience for the prices; a coffee costs about twice what it does at home, which is easier to accept once you have tasted the cinnamon buns.
Next time I will take the coastal railway further north, to Bodø, and continue by boat, though everyone I met warned me that the winter crossing is not for the faint-hearted.
